The method operates in two phases: bounding box determination and sample filtering [S1, S2].

The claim states the method operates in two phases: 'bounding box determination' and 'sample filtering'. Source [S1] explicitly describes these two strategies: locating the smallest bounding box (bounding box determination) and filtering out sampled points recognized as empty (sample filtering). However, Source [S2] describes a different set of optimizations: 'Ray skipping' (which uses a bounding box) and 'Voxel skipping' (which uses a mask volume). While 'Ray skipping' is related to bounding boxes, 'Voxel skipping' is distinct from 'sample filtering' as described in [S1] (which filters points based on alpha values during ray marching). Furthermore, the claim implies a specific two-phase structure ('bounding box determination and sample filtering') which matches [S1] well but does not accurately summarize [S2]'s 'Ray skipping' and 'Voxel skipping' phases. Since the evidence from [S2] describes different mechanisms (specifically voxel skipping vs sample filtering) and the claim presents a unified two-phase description that doesn't fully align with the distinct terminology and mechanisms in [S2], the evidence only partially supports the specific phrasing of the claim across both sources.
